newsitem.title: USA: U.S West Coast crudes slip amid heating oil build.
newsitem.headline: U.S West Coast crudes slip amid heating oil build.

text.p: U.S. West Coast crudes slipped Friday as spot trade remained quiet and NYMEX fell on a build in heating oil supplies, traders said.
Heating oil for February was down 0.31 cents a gallon at 1117 PST, after a late Thursday report showed distillates grew by a significant 2.5 million barrels last week
Spot trade of Alaska North Slope (ANS) crude continued to languish following a mid-week holiday.
But business for February barrels of ANS was expected to pick up next week, as refiners prepared for next month's production.
"We expect to be on the market for a couple of cargoes," said a trader for a major West Coast refiner.
With activity low, discounts for ANS stayed at $1.70 under West Texas Intermediate (WTI), the U.S. benchmark oil.
Outright ANS values fell in line with a 20-cent drop in WTI, ranging $23.55/23.75 a barrel.
Line 63 crude remained untraded off WTI, while the posting plus market was notionally $0.95 to $1.05.
Traders said spring maintenance at a handful of regional refiners would flood the market with unprocessed heavy oil.
"I imagine the heavy market will take a big dumb," a trader said.
Units will come off line at Exxon's Benecia plant, Tosco's Avon, Calif., facility, and Mobil's Torrance plant, traders said.
Meanwhile, heavy crude were unchanged. Kern River prices stayed at $18.65/18.75 a barrel after companies lifted postings December 18.
Discounts remained 10 cents below to even with postings, traders said.
